TWO SPIKES RUN, TWO NOT RUN, and I am recording which is which rather than presenting four results.

SP4 — DOES THE PACKAGED BINARY RESOLVE, AND IS ITS FAILURE LOUD? RUN (run-9406dd97f88c). 20-minute timebox, took under a minute.
  RESULT, both halves: the binary resolves to a per-platform sub-package and executes — ripgrep 15.0.0. And the deliberate failure is LOUD: a missing binary raises ENOENT at spawn, immediately, naming the path.
  FOLDED UPSTREAM: this is the first OBSERVATION of the property the whole M5 convergence rests on. The deciding argument was that the chosen design fails loudly and once while the rival fails silently and late. Until now the loud half was asserted. It is now measured, and the M5 decision is correspondingly better supported than when it was made.
  ALSO FOLDED: the resolution path is a per-platform sub-package rather than a download, which sharpens tripwire T1 — the failure mode to watch is 'no sub-package published for this platform', not 'the network was unavailable at install'.

SP3 — THE PARSER AT ITS EDGES. RUN (run-9406dd97f88c). 30-minute timebox, took under a minute.
  CASES: a path with a space, a file with no trailing newline, a 3000-character line, a nested path, a binary file. A path containing a COLON was not tested and cannot be — it is illegal on this platform. Recorded rather than faked; on other platforms it remains untested and it is the sharpest case for the rival design, whose ref output packs a ref and a path into one colon-joined field.
  RESULT — THE CHOSEN DESIGN: typed events for every case, correct paths for spaces and nesting, the long line reported at its true length, and the binary file SKIPPED silently by default. No wrong answers.
  RESULT — THE REAL FINDING: version-control grep, run WITHOUT the binary-exclusion flag, emits 'Binary file X matches' as a line with NO field structure at all. A parser splitting on the field separator gets one element where it expects three. That is a wrong-shape record reaching a parser that believes it has a contract — exactly the failure class this architecture was chosen to avoid.
  FOLDED UPSTREAM, and this is the part worth keeping: our implementation ALREADY passes the binary-exclusion flag, so the hazard does not reach us. What the spike changes is that the flag is now known to be LOAD-BEARING rather than tidy. It had no recorded reason; removing it would look like a harmless simplification and would silently break ref search on any repository containing a binary file.
  ALSO FOLDED: this strengthens the M4 scoring of structured output with evidence rather than argument. The rival's parsing risk is not hypothetical — one flag away is a malformed record.

SP1 — THE APPLICABILITY SELECTOR. NOT RUN. Timeboxed at 90 minutes, and it is the highest-ranked unknown in the iteration.
  WHY NOT: it is the largest spike by a wide margin and it requires a hand-written answer key BEFORE any selection is run, or the exercise is worthless. Rushing it inside the remaining budget would produce the one outcome its own kill condition forbids — picking the least-bad vocabulary and calling it settled.
  CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: R14's mechanism is NOT decided by this iteration. The requirement stands, the decision node names three candidate vocabularies, and the selector remains unchosen. Three of the five at-risk quality scenarios stay at risk. This is the largest single thing this iteration does not deliver, and it is carried forward openly rather than dressed as partial progress.

SP2 — REOPEN AS A PROPERTY. NOT RUN as a property test. Timeboxed at 60 minutes.
  WHY NOT: the two known failure shapes are covered by five example tests written today, both with red observed before green. What is missing is the generative version — the one whose bar was 'this test, written yesterday, catches today's two bugs'.
  CONSEQUENCE: reopen keeps its at-risk verdict from the architecture evaluation. Our record of reasoning about this property unaided is 0 for 2, and example tests encode only the failures already met. Carried to the build as the first fitness function rather than dropped.

NO UPSTREAM REOPEN IS TRIGGERED. Both run spikes CONFIRMED the design rather than invalidating it, so nothing upstream is suspect and nothing is reopened. Recording that explicitly, because 'no ripple' should be a finding rather than a silence — the two spikes that could have overturned the M5 decision were the two that were run, and neither did.
payload.promotions:
MARKED FOR ENTRY INTO THE BUILD:

P1 — A TEST PINNING THE BINARY-EXCLUSION FLAG ON REF SEARCH. From SP3, and the clearest promotion of the four.
  WHAT: assert that a ref search over a repository containing a binary file returns well-formed records only — never a record with a missing field.
  WHY IT MUST BE A TEST AND NOT A COMMENT: the flag currently looks like a tidy default with no stated reason. A future reader simplifying the argument list would remove it, the parser would receive a one-field line where it expects three, and ref search would break on any repository with a binary in it. This is the project's own rule applied — a deliberate choice that must survive future edits gets a test, not a comment.

P2 — THE REOPEN PROPERTY TEST. From SP2, unrun.
  WHAT: generate reopens across the real machine's states; assert every state in the cone stays reachable and no state re-activates itself.
  WHY IT LEADS THE FITNESS LIST: it is the only candidate that would have caught defects we did not already have. The five existing tests are memorials to two specific bugs.

P3 — THE GATE-ROUNDS PROPERTY. Named at the architecture evaluation as fitness candidate one.
  WHAT: compile the machine and assert every gate state carries all four rounds as required.
  WHY: it is a property over the WHOLE machine, trivially computable, and it guards the iteration's central claim against the exact way that claim was broken before — a gate authored later, differently, that quietly misses them.

NOT PROMOTED, and named so the absence is deliberate:
  THE APPLICABILITY SELECTOR. Nothing from SP1 enters the build, because SP1 did not run. Building a selector on an unmeasured vocabulary would be the guessed-selector outcome its own kill condition forbids, and a wrong selector is worse than a missing one because it looks like coverage.
  THE COLON-IN-PATH CASE. Untestable on this platform. It stays an open edge for the rival design, and it matters only if tripwire T1 ever fires and the fallback is taken — at which point it must be tested first.
